title: Is confidence inversely calibrated?
whyPreRegistered: The four measurements below are fixed BEFORE the pilot runs, which is the whole point of a pilot charter: it prevents anyone retrospectively finding the metric that makes the result look successful. Nothing in this file may be edited once the pilot is running. If a criterion turns out to be wrong, the pilot is KILLED and a PILOT-002 is registered with the corrected criterion and a new baseline - it is not quietly amended.
hypothesis: Confidence is INVERSELY calibrated on this account: trades entered at 85%+ confidence return a worse realised R per trade than trades entered at 65-74%. If true, the highest-confidence signals are the worst ones, and raising confidenceThreshold would concentrate trading into the losing tier.
nullHypothesis: The 85%+ tier's mean realised R is not distinguishable from zero, or is not worse than the 65-74% tier. Confidence carries no reliable signal about payoff either way.

primaryOutcomeMetric.name: avgRealizedR of the 85%+ confidence tier
primaryOutcomeMetric.definition: mean of realizedRFromPrices(direction, entry, sl, closePrice) over CLOSED journal fills whose confidence >= 85
primaryOutcomeMetric.whyThisOne: R, not dollars. Lot sizes on this account have varied 38x across the live record and were pinned by fixedLotSize and by the broker volume_min on most fills, so dollars measure the sizing pipeline rather than the setup. Win rate is excluded as a primary metric for the reason this pilot exists: it cannot see payoff at all.

baseline.measuredFrom: laptop journal, 24 closed fills spanning 48 days (0.50 fills/day overall)
baseline.note: The VPS is a SEPARATE account with its own journal and is recorded here as an independent replication, not pooled. Pooling them would inflate the row count without adding information - the two boxes run the same config on the same bars.

peerReplication.why: The direction of the effect reproduces on an independent account with a LARGER top-tier sample (n=13 vs 6). That is corroboration, not proof - same engine, same bars, same config.

minimumViableTarget.value: 85+ tier reaches n >= 37 with its mean realised R still below zero
minimumViableTarget.derivation: n = (1.96 * sd / |mean|)^2 = (1.96 * 1.209 / 0.391)^2 = 37 fills, the sample needed to separate the observed mean from zero at 95%. DERIVED from the observed effect and dispersion, NOT chosen. A target picked by hand is the failure this pre-registration exists to prevent.
minimumViableTarget.deliberatelyNotTheSystemBar: tasks/lab_promote.cjs sets MIN_TRADES = 100 per cell for PROMOTING a strategy. That bar is not used here and the difference is stated rather than hidden: at the 85+ tier's observed rate of 0.125 fills/day, 100 fills is roughly 800 days - far outside MAX_DAYS_TO_PROOF. This pilot is powered to answer its question, not to promote a strategy. Clearing it justifies a walk-forward, NOT a gate change.

guardrails.why: What is not allowed to get worse while the pilot runs. Any breach ends the pilot immediately - a pilot that damages the system it is measuring has already failed regardless of its result.

items.rule: The set of setups that fire must not shrink. No signal may be suppressed to make the tiers look cleaner.
items.check: diff /api/signals before and after any change

items.rule: confidenceThreshold must remain 70 for the duration. Changing the gate mid-pilot destroys the baseline and the pilot with it.
The journal, the shadow ledgers and the calibration record must keep accumulating. Sample size is the binding constraint; anything that slows it costs more than this pilot can return.
Backfilled executor rows stay OUT of learning. They are historical and scoring them would rewrite the calibration record this pilot measures.
items.check: reconciliation.unscoredByDesign continues to account for them

timebox.derivation: 37 fills needed / 0.125 fills per day observed in the 85+ tier = 294 days
timebox.hardStopSource: tasks/lab_promote.cjs MAX_DAYS_TO_PROOF - 'A candidate that cannot be settled inside a year is not a finding, it is a permanent maybe.'
timebox.note: 294 is INSIDE the 365 bar, but not by much, and it assumes the trade rate holds. If the rate falls the pilot expires unproven, and that is a real outcome to be reported rather than extended.

goNoGo.go: 85+ tier at n >= 37 with mean R < 0 AND below the 65-74% tier: the effect is real at this sample. NEXT STEP IS A WALK-FORWARD, not a gate change - a tier table is not a walk-forward and loses to one wherever they disagree.
goNoGo.noGo: 85+ tier at n >= 37 with mean R indistinguishable from zero, or not worse than 65-74%: hypothesis killed, recorded as measured-and-false, and confidence is left alone.
goNoGo.expired: 365 days reached without n >= 37: reported as UNPROVEN at this trade rate. Not a failure of the hypothesis - a statement that this system cannot answer it at its current sample rate, which is itself the most useful thing the pilot can say.

whatWouldChangeTheAnswer: A sizing change during the pilot. R is sizing-independent by construction, but a lot-size change that alters WHICH setups fill would change the population being measured.
The gate moving off 70. The tiers are defined relative to a gate at 70; move it and the 65-74 tier partly stops existing.
A new setup entering the 85+ tier in volume. The tier is a mix of setups, not one strategy, and a single new high-confidence setup could dominate it.
notes: PILOT-001 is a measurement, not a change. It places no order, moves no threshold and modifies no code. Its only output is a verdict and the evidence behind it.
